parameters.content:
Consider these changes to build dynamic pose prompt if needed:

What to trim from your current POSE map:

Pose 3: remove style lines like “Skin tones must always match.” Keep visor specifics.

Pose 6: remove “Eyes must always have iris and pupil” (already covered globally).

Pose 9: remove “No visible teeth” if you enforce “no teeth” globally.

Pose 11: keep “NO ARMS HANG by the sides” (that’s kinematic), remove any style bits if present.

3) Outline / line-weight lock

Your goal was to avoid adopting the bold mannequin outline from POSE. You already have the strong negative: “No black stroke outline.” That’s usually sufficient.

If you start seeing style drift (thicker/thinner lines vs BASE) across batches, add a soft version back:

“Line work must match BASE (overall weight/feel). Do not add heavy outlines or vary thickness.”
This keeps you anchored to BASE without over-constraining.

Minimal, surgical edits I’d make now

A) Global facial schema (in Build Prompt’s STYLE DNA / FACIAL block)

FACIAL/FEATURE SCHEMA (copy from BASE):
- Eyes: iris + pupil, match BASE shape/size/spacing. Never omit irises.
- Nose: small filled triangle (orientation/size like BASE).
- Mouth: simple short curve; no teeth or lips.
- Cheeks: circular blush discs if present in BASE; same placement/size/opacity.


B) Remove style lines from POSE_PROMPT_MAP (keep only pose/gesture/stance specifics). For example:

Pose 3: keep visor hand + orientation; drop skin-tone/eye notes.

Pose 6: drop the eye/skin notes (already global).

Pose 9: rely on global “no teeth.”

Pose 11: keep “no arms hang by sides”; drop any style notes.

C) Keep your hair language exactly as you have it

BASE controls hair color; HAIR CHIP = silhouette only; if silhouette conflicts with POSE geometry, adjust silhouette to fit POSE. This is perfect.

D) Optional soft line-work guard (only if drift appears)

- Line work must match BASE’s general weight/feel; never adopt the mannequin’s bold stroke.
